request.spec:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each claim now shows its status log, and all 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

Each line reads `<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>`, oldest first. A line is written when the claim is added (DRAFT) and on every status change: open, settle, void, a settle that goes to PENDING, approve (SETTLED) and reject (back to OPEN). Quick-add and bulk-open go through the same code, so they write lines too.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V30__claim_log.sql`, adds a `claim_log` table. Each row holds the claim, the status, who made the change, the sheet's today at the time, and the due. The due is saved as text so "n/a" can be stored as is.

**Server:**
- `ClaimLog` and `ClaimLogRepository` are new.
- `ClaimService` writes a log line in the same transaction as each change, so a refused change writes no log line.
- The due in each line is worked out the way the screen shows it: the settled due if the claim has one, otherwise its current figure plus any late charge. It's taken just after the status changes.
- The claim data the API returns now includes the log. The claims list fetches every log line for the sheet in one query.

**Front end:** the claims table in `claims.ts` has a new "Log" column with one `claim-log-line` item per line.

Claims that existed before this migration start with an empty log; nothing fills in their history. That only matters for a database that persists, and this one is in-memory and starts empty on every run.
